attachment.content:
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review changed code for reuse, quality, and efficiency, then fix any issues found.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled remote agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring remote agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Build, debug, and optimize Claude API / Anthropic SDK apps. Apps built with this skill should include prompt caching. Also handles migrating existing Claude API code between Claude model versions (4.5 → 4.6, 4.6 → 4.7, retired-model replacements).
TRIGGER when: code imports `anthropic`/`@anthropic-ai/sdk`; user asks for the Claude API, Anthropic SDK, or Managed Agents; user adds/modifies/tunes a Claude feature (caching, thinking, compaction, tool use, batch, files, citations, memory) or model (Opus/Sonnet/Haiku) in a file; questions about prompt caching / cache hit rate in an Anthropic SDK project.
SKIP: file imports `openai`/other-provider SDK, filename like `*-openai.py`/`*-generic.py`, provider-neutral code, general programming/ML.
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a pull request
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

1	# §4 Experiments
2	
3	## §4.1 Experimental Setup
4	
5	**Dataset.** We construct a code retrieval dataset from SWE-smith \cite{yang2025swesmith}, a large-scale collection of synthetic Python bug-fix instances derived from real-world GitHub repositories. After excluding repositories with failed clones, 44,173 instances across 123 repositories remain. Our structural extraction pipeline (\S3.2) produces inter-procedural data-flow graphs for 15,897 instances (36.0\%); of these, 14,288 yield resolvable positive files and are retained for training. Per-seed stratified splits produce $\sim$11,300 training and $\sim$3,000 validation instances, preserving repository-level distribution across partitions.
6	
7	**Encoders.** We select two 3B-parameter decoder-only code models representing distinct pretraining paradigms: **Qwen2.5-Coder-3B** \cite{hui2024qwen25coder} (Fill-in-the-Middle on curated multilingual code) and **StarCoder2-3B** \cite{lozhkov2024starcoder2} (multi-task FIM on The Stack v2). These encoders exhibit markedly different pretrained representation geometries: Qwen operates in a near-saturated similarity regime (mean positive cosine similarity 0.986), while StarCoder maintains healthy separation (0.799). This divergence enables examination of whether mining strategy effectiveness interacts with encoder properties---a core question of our study.
8	
9	**Training.** All fine-tuning details follow \S3.4: LoRA ($r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$) on $W_q$/$W_v$, InfoNCE with learnable $\tau$, AdamW ($\text{lr}{=}2{\times}10^{-5}$). Seed 42 trains for 3 epochs without early stopping to provide a full overfitting diagnostic curve; seeds 43 and 44 train for 2 epochs with early stopping (patience 2, evaluated every 500 steps).\footnote{The 3-epoch seed-42 runs enable analysis of post-peak degradation (\S4.3.3); all checkpoint selection uses the same dual-checkpoint protocol regardless of epoch count.} We maintain dual checkpoints per run: $\theta^*_{\text{loss}}$ (best validation loss) and $\theta^*_{\text{R@1}}$ (best validation Recall@1).
10	
11	**Evaluation.** Pool-based retrieval with pool size 50 (1 positive + 49 negatives). Primary metric: Recall@1 (R@1)---whether the top-ranked file is a gold patch target. We report $\theta^*_{\text{R@1}}$ as the primary result; fixed-checkpoint ($\theta^*_{\text{loss}}$) comparisons appear in Table~2 as a robustness check.
12	
13	**Seeds.** Each encoder $\times$ strategy combination is trained with 3 random seeds (42, 43, 44), yielding $2 \times 3 \times 3 = 18$ total runs. We report bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals for all pairwise comparisons.
14

# §4 Experiments

## §4.1 Experimental Setup

**Dataset.** We construct a code retrieval dataset from SWE-smith \cite{yang2025swesmith}, a large-scale collection of synthetic Python bug-fix instances derived from real-world GitHub repositories. After excluding repositories with failed clones, 44,173 instances across 123 repositories remain. Our structural extraction pipeline (\S3.2) produces inter-procedural data-flow graphs for 15,897 instances (36.0\%); of these, 14,288 yield resolvable positive files and are retained for training. Per-seed stratified splits produce $\sim$11,300 training and $\sim$3,000 validation instances, preserving repository-level distribution across partitions.

**Encoders.** We select two 3B-parameter decoder-only code models representing distinct pretraining paradigms: **Qwen2.5-Coder-3B** \cite{hui2024qwen25coder} (Fill-in-the-Middle on curated multilingual code) and **StarCoder2-3B** \cite{lozhkov2024starcoder2} (multi-task FIM on The Stack v2). These encoders exhibit markedly different pretrained representation geometries: Qwen operates in a near-saturated similarity regime (mean positive cosine similarity 0.986), while StarCoder maintains healthy separation (0.799). This divergence enables examination of whether mining strategy effectiveness interacts with encoder properties---a core question of our study.

**Training.** All fine-tuning details follow \S3.4: LoRA ($r{=}16$, $\alpha{=}32$) on $W_q$/$W_v$, InfoNCE with learnable $\tau$, AdamW ($\text{lr}{=}2{\times}10^{-5}$). Seed 42 trains for 3 epochs without early stopping to provide a full overfitting diagnostic curve; seeds 43 and 44 train for 2 epochs with early stopping (patience 2, evaluated every 500 steps).\footnote{The 3-epoch seed-42 runs enable analysis of post-peak degradation (\S4.3.3); all checkpoint selection uses the same dual-checkpoint protocol regardless of epoch count.} We maintain dual checkpoints per run: $\theta^*_{\text{loss}}$ (best validation loss) and $\theta^*_{\text{R@1}}$ (best validation Recall@1).

**Evaluation.** Pool-based retrieval with pool size 50 (1 positive + 49 negatives). Primary metric: Recall@1 (R@1)---whether the top-ranked file is a gold patch target. We report $\theta^*_{\text{R@1}}$ as the primary result; fixed-checkpoint ($\theta^*_{\text{loss}}$) comparisons appear in Table~2 as a robustness check.

**Seeds.** Each encoder $\times$ strategy combination is trained with 3 random seeds (42, 43, 44), yielding $2 \times 3 \times 3 = 18$ total runs. We report bootstrap 95\% confidence intervals for all pairwise comparisons.

### 建议
1. experiments_v1.md 的统计方法描述需明确写出 cluster bootstrap by repo，不能留 generic bootstrap——这是 D055 的核心改动，也是论文方法论的关键细节
2. 表格中 pool=8 的数字要么标注为 provisional，要么等 pool=50 评估完成后再填入——避免 caption 和数据源不一致

Instance-level cluster bootstrap: embedding_distance vs random mining (s43).
Evaluates both checkpoints on val_random_s43.jsonl (common eval set),
computes per-instance R@1, and runs cluster bootstrap clustered by repo.
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import time
import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
from pathlib import Path
from collections import defaultdict

sys.path.insert(0, "/root/structfuse/training")
from contrastive_model import StructFuseEncoder
from transformers import AutoTokenizer

RANDOM_CKPT = "/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/checkpoints/m2_full_qwen/random_s43/best_by_recall_at_1"
EMBED_CKPT = "/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/checkpoints/m2_full_qwen/embedding_distance_s43/best_by_recall_at_1"
BASE_MODEL = "/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/models/Qwen/Qwen2.5-Coder-3B"
VAL_FILE = "/root/autodl-tmp/structfuse/full_m2_training_data/val_random_s43.jsonl"
DEVICE = "cuda:0"
MAX_SEQ_LEN = 2048
NUM_NEGATIVES = 7
ENCODE_BATCH = 8
N_BOOTSTRAP = 10000
OUTPUT_PATH = "/root/structfuse/results/bootstrap_s43_paired.json"


def load_model(ckpt_dir, base_model, device):
    config_path = Path(ckpt_dir) / "training_config.json"
    with open(config_path) as f:
        cfg = json.load(f)
    model = StructFuseEncoder(
        model_name=base_model,
        proj_dim=cfg.get("proj_dim", 256),
        use_lora=cfg.get("use_lora", True),
        lora_r=cfg.get("lora_r", 16),
        use_fusion_head=cfg.get("use_fusion_head", False),
    )
    state_dict = torch.load(Path(ckpt_dir) / "model.pt", map_location="cpu")
    result = model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=False)
    assert not result.missing_keys, f"Missing keys: {result.missing_keys}"
    model = model.to(device).eval()
    return model


def load_val_data(val_file, num_negatives):
    samples = []
    with open(val_file) as f:
        for line in f:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            d = json.loads(line)
            neg_candidates = d.get("neg_candidates", [])
            candidate_tokens = d.get("candidate_tokens", {})
            neg_texts = []
            for cid in neg_candidates:
                t = candidate_tokens.get(cid, "")
                if t:
                    neg_texts.append(t)
                if len(neg_texts) >= num_negatives:
                    break
            pool_texts = [d["pos_tokens"]] + neg_texts
            samples.append({
                "query_id": d["query_id"],
                "query_text": d["query_tokens"],
                "pool_texts": pool_texts,
            })
    return samples


def batch_encode(model, tokenizer, texts, device, max_len, batch_size):
    all_embs = []
    for i in range(0, len(texts), batch_size):
        batch = texts[i:i+batch_size]
        enc = tokenizer(batch, truncation=True, max_length=max_len,
                       padding=True, return_tensors="pt")
        enc = {k: v.to(device) for k, v in enc.items()}
        with torch.no_grad():
            emb = model.encode(enc["input_ids"], enc["attention_mask"])

    print(f"\n{'='*60}", flush=True)
    print("Model 1: random_s43", flush=True)

    print(f"R@1 = {np.mean(r1_random):.4f}", flush=True)
    del model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # Model 2: embedding_distance_s43
    print(f"\n{'='*60}", flush=True)
    print("Model 2: embedding_distance_s43", flush=True)
    model = load_model(EMBED_CKPT, BASE_MODEL, DEVICE)

    print(f"R@1 = {np.mean(r1_embed):.4f}", flush=True)
    del model
    torch.cuda.empty_cache()

    # Paired analysis
    query_ids = [s["query_id"] for s in samples]
    repo_ids = [extract_repo(qid) for qid in query_ids]
    deltas = [e - r for e, r in zip(r1_embed, r1_random)]
    unique_repos = sorted(set(repo_ids))

    n_better = sum(1 for d in deltas if d > 0)
    n_worse = sum(1 for d in deltas if d < 0)
    n_tied = sum(1 for d in deltas if d == 0)

    print(f"\n{'='*60}", flush=True)
    print("Paired Analysis", flush=True)

    print(f"\nCluster bootstrap ({N_BOOTSTRAP} iterations)...", flush=True)

def parse_train_log(log_path: str) -> List[dict]:
    """Parse [eval@step] and [Final eval] lines from a train log."""
    results = []
    eval_pat = re.compile(r"\[eval@(\d+)\]\s*(\{.*\})")
    final_pat = re.compile(r"\[Final eval\]\s*(\{.*\})")
    best_r1_pat = re.compile(r"New best R@1=([\d.]+)")

    best_r1_value = None
    with open(log_path) as f:
        for line in f:
            m = eval_pat.search(line)
            if m:
                step = int(m.group(1))
                try:
                    metrics = ast.literal_eval(m.group(2))
                    metrics["step"] = step
                    metrics["source"] = "eval"
                    results.append(metrics)

            m = final_pat.search(line)
            if m:

                    metrics["step"] = -1
                    metrics["source"] = "final"
                    results.append(metrics)
                except (ValueError, SyntaxError):
                    pass
                continue
            m = best_r1_pat.search(line)
            if m:
                best_r1_value = float(m.group(1))

    return results


def get_best_r1_from_log(log_path: str) -> Optional[dict]:
    """Extract best R@1 checkpoint info from a train log."""
